name: Cool Green
lede: Cool Green is a plain descriptive name for a fresh green that leans slightly toward blue; the swatch here comes from a 2010 online color survey, not from any older system.

sections.title: Cool, in a painter's sense
sections.body:
The name is a modifier plus a color word, not a historic color [1]. Its swatch is listed in the xkcd color survey of 2010, and the nearest ISCC-NBS name is "vivid green", 8.2 units away [1]. Painters use *cool* for a color that leans toward blue and away from yellow, so a cool green sits nearer [[emerald]] and [[viridian]] than [[olive-green]].

The pairing is old as a way of talking about pictures. Ball describes the engraver Jacob Christoph Le Blon's print *Narcissus* as combining warm flesh tones with cool green foliage [2].

sections.title: An old experiment
sections.body: Birren reports a mid-century clinical setup in which a room overlooking a garden was lit in two colors, a warm red and a cool green, while a patient sat alone for a quarter or half an hour and was then questioned about mood and associations [3]. Birren's claims about color and health are old opinion, not modern evidence, so the passage is a record of what was tried and no proof that a color treats anything [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our archive of 23,781 has this color covering at least 1 per cent of its canvas, within four units of CIEDE2000 [4]. That describes our archive of photographed museum paintings, not painting as a whole; a pure mid green is rare on canvas [4]. The color measures lightness 66, chroma 63 and hue 149 in CIELCH [1].

questions.q: What does a painter mean by a cool green?
choices: A green with grey in it

questions.q: True or false: Cool Green is a historic pigment name.

openers: Cool and warm are painter's words for lean: a green toward blue is cool, toward yellow is warm.
